r1-dependency-2.summary: Retrieved recent deployments, configuration changes, feature flags, and infrastructure changes over a 7-day window and mapped the service dependency graph for orders-service and mobile-bff. A notable marketing campaign event (diwali_sip_offer) occurred at 13:30, just two minutes before the reported symptom onset.

findings.statement: orders-service depends synchronously on broker-api and portfolio-db, and is called synchronously by mobile-bff.
mobile-bff calls auth-service, payments-api, portfolio-service, orders-service, kyc-service, and aa-connector synchronously.
notification-service launched the 'diwali_sip_offer' push campaign to 2.1M users with deep link 'orders/new-sip' at 2026-10-10T13:30:00+00:00 (chg-9674).
market-data-service v2.12.0 and user-db v3.23.0 were deployed shortly before the incident at 12:39 and 12:40 on 2026-10-10.

open_questions: Did the high-volume push campaign at 13:30 cause a sudden traffic surge leading to resource exhaustion or rate-limiting in orders-service or broker-api?

r1-observability-1.summary: orders-service and mobile-bff experienced a sudden traffic surge starting at 13:31 UTC, followed immediately by error rate spikes at 13:32 UTC. orders-service suffered thread pool saturation (RejectedExecutionException: order-executor queue full) causing p99 latency to spike to ~9s and error rates to peak at 15.85%. mobile-bff error rates also spiked up to 4.42%.

findings.statement: orders-service experienced an RPS anomaly onset starting at 2026-10-10T13:31:00+00:00, surging from a baseline of ~115 req/s to a peak of 872.67 req/s.
orders-service error rate and latency anomalies began at 2026-10-10T13:32:00+00:00, with error rates peaking at 15.85% and p99 latency peaking at 8,999.2 ms.
orders-service started logging RejectedExecutionException due to order-executor queue full (capacity 500) starting at 2026-10-10T13:32:04+00:00.
mobile-bff experienced an RPS anomaly starting at 2026-10-10T13:31:00+00:00 and an error rate anomaly starting at 13:32:00+00:00, peaking at 4.42% error rate.
orders-service CPU usage spiked up to 106.54% and reached maximum autoscaler replicas (6/6) at 13:50:19.

open_questions: What caused the sudden traffic surge (RPS increase) across mobile-bff and orders-service at 13:31 UTC?

r2-observability-1.summary: Retrieved health metrics and logs for notification-service around the 13:30 push campaign window (13:25 to 13:40). Telemetry shows notification-service resource utilization and performance remained completely normal with no anomalies in CPU, memory, RPS, error rate, or latency.

findings.statement: notification-service CPU usage remained stable around 39% with no anomaly during the push campaign window.
notification-service memory usage remained steady between 49.2% and 63.94% with no anomaly in the window.
notification-service error rate and p99 latency showed no anomalies during the push campaign window.
notification-service logs confirm successful dispatch of the Push campaign diwali_sip_offer starting at 13:30.

r2-observability-2.summary: Orders-service experienced an anomaly starting at 13:31 with a sudden surge in traffic (RPS) and CPU usage, followed by execution queue exhaustion (order-executor queue full capacity 500) and increased error rates starting at 13:32.

findings.statement: orders-service rps anomaly started up from 13:31, reaching a peak of 872.67 req/s at 13:44.
orders-service cpu_pct anomaly started up from 13:31, reaching a peak of 106.54% at 13:47.
orders-service error_rate_pct anomaly started up from 13:32, reaching a peak of 15.85% at 13:43.
orders-service latency_p99_ms anomaly started up from 13:32, reaching a peak of 8999.2 ms at 13:42.
orders-service logged RejectedExecutionException: order-executor queue full (capacity 500) starting at 13:32.

open_questions: What caused the abrupt spike in traffic (RPS) on orders-service starting at 13:31?

hypotheses.title: Diwali SIP Campaign Push Notification Traffic Surge
hypotheses.mechanism: The notification-service triggered a push campaign at 13:30 to 2.1M users with a deep link to 'orders/new-sip'. This prompted a synchronized user influx starting at 13:31 across mobile-bff and orders-service. The resulting traffic surge overwhelmed orders-service's internal executor queue (capacity 500), leading to RejectedExecutionException errors, latency spikes, and failed order placements starting at 13:32.

supporting.note: Push campaign sent to 2.1M users at 13:30, precisely preceding the 13:31 traffic surge onset.
Notification service logs confirm dispatch of the push campaign at 13:30.
Shows sudden RPS increase starting at 13:31.
Shows sudden RPS increase starting at 13:31, surging from baseline 115 req/s to 748+ req/s.
orders-service logged RejectedExecutionException due to order-executor queue full starting at 13:32.
Notification-service health metrics retrieved and verified stable during campaign window.
Notification-service memory usage verified stable during campaign window.
Notification-service error rate verified stable during campaign window.
Notification-service latency verified stable during campaign window.

assumptions: The push notification deep link successfully drove immediate concurrent user sessions that exceeded provisioned orders-service baseline capacity before autoscaling took full effect.

hypotheses.title: Broker-API Rate Limiting / Downstream Bottleneck
hypotheses.mechanism: Upstream broker-api rate-limiting or congestion caused requests inside orders-service to block and back up, saturating the executor thread pool and leading to RejectedExecutionException errors.

supporting.note: orders-service previously received 429 Too Many Requests from broker-api.

contradicting.note: Broker-API 429 warnings occurred earlier at 12:31, whereas the incident onset and massive RPS surge strictly correlate with the 13:30 push campaign.

assumptions: Broker-api experienced unlogged rate-limiting right at 13:31 coinciding with normal traffic.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Symptom onset is clearly established at 13:31 for RPS and 13:32 for error rates and latency. Following the Critic's review, notification-service health metrics and logs were retrieved, confirming that notification-service operated normally while successfully dispatching the high-volume push campaign (chg-9674) at 13:30. This campaign directly drove the simultaneous traffic surge at 13:31, overwhelming orders-service's execution capacity. H1 confidence is raised due to verified health telemetry of notification-service and complete timing alignment.
